source.text: וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ דָּוִד֙ מִשָּׁ֔ם וַיִּמָּלֵ֖ט אֶל־מְעָרַ֣ת עֲדֻלָּ֑ם וַיִּשְׁמְע֤וּ אֶחָיו֙ וְכָל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔יו וַיֵּרְד֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו שָֽׁמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went David from there and escaped to [the] cave of Adullam; and heard [it] his brothers and all [the] house of his father, and went down to him there.

en.L: And David went from there and escaped to the cave of Adullam. And his brothers and all his father's house heard [it], and they went down to him there.
en.B: David left that place and got away to the cave of Adullam. His brothers and his father's whole family heard about it, and they went down to join him there.
en.R: David left Gath and escaped to the cave of Adullam. His brothers and the rest of his father's family heard where he was, and they went down to him there.

es.L: Y se fue David de allí y escapó a la cueva de Adulam. Y [lo] oyeron sus hermanos y toda la casa de su padre, y bajaron allá a él.
es.B: David salió de allí y se refugió en la cueva de Adulam. Sus hermanos y toda la familia de su padre se enteraron y bajaron allá para unirse a él.
es.R: David se fue de Gat y escapó a la cueva de Adulam. Sus hermanos y el resto de la familia de su padre se enteraron de dónde estaba, y bajaron allá a reunirse con él.

fr.L: Et David partit de là et se réfugia dans la grotte d’Adoullam. Et ses frères et toute la maison de son père [l’]apprirent, et ils descendirent là vers lui.
fr.B: David quitta ce lieu et se mit à l’abri dans la grotte d’Adoullam. Ses frères et toute la famille de son père l’apprirent, et ils descendirent le rejoindre là.
fr.R: David a quitté Gath et il s’est réfugié dans la grotte d’Adoullam. Ses frères et le reste de la famille de son père ont appris où il était, et ils sont descendus le rejoindre là-bas.

vi.L: Đa-vít đi khỏi đó và trốn đến hang A-đu-lam. Các anh của ông và cả nhà cha ông nghe [tin], thì xuống đó với ông.
vi.B: Đa-vít rời khỏi nơi ấy và trốn đến hang A-đu-lam. Các anh ông và cả gia đình cha ông nghe tin thì xuống đó với ông.
vi.R: Đa-vít rời Gát và trốn đến hang A-đu-lam. Các anh ông và cả gia đình cha ông nghe biết ông ở đâu, nên họ xuống đó với ông.

decisions.choice: the cave of Adullam: a cave near the town of Adullam in the lowland hills of Judah
decisions.reason: Adullam was a town in the low hill country west of Bethlehem (Joshua 15:33-35). The limestone hills there are full of caves where a band of men could hide. David is back in the territory of his own tribe, out of the reach of the Philistines.

decisions.choice: from there: from Gath
decisions.reason: The last place named is Gath, where David had pretended to be mad before King Achish (21:11-16). He now leaves Philistine territory.

decisions.choice: his family joins him: the household of a fugitive was in danger too
decisions.reason: A king who hunted a man could punish his relatives as well, as Saul does to Ahimelech's whole family later in this chapter (verses 16-19). They "went down" because Bethlehem lies higher in the hills than Adullam.

decisions.choice: the cave: the setting named in the titles of two psalms
decisions.reason: The titles of Psalm 57 and Psalm 142 link those prayers to the time when David was in the cave. The titles do not say which cave, and 24:4 tells of another cave where David hid.

decisions.choice: Gath
decisions.reason: Readable names the place "there" points back to, so the reader does not need to look back to the end of chapter 21.

decisions.choice: la grotte d'Adoullam
decisions.reason: A name not in the terms table, in the usual French transcription, kept the same through both books.

decisions.choice: la cueva de Adulam
decisions.reason: The usual Spanish form of the place name (m1); it stays the same in 2 Samuel 23:13.

source.text: וַיִּֽתְקַבְּצ֣וּ אֵ֠לָיו כָּל־אִ֨ישׁ מָצ֜וֹק וְכָל־אִ֨ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ל֤וֹ נֹשֶׁא֙ וְכָל־אִ֣ישׁ מַר־נֶ֔פֶשׁ וַיְהִ֥י עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לְשָׂ֑ר וַיִּהְי֣וּ עִמּ֔וֹ כְּאַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת אִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And gathered to him every man of distress, and every man who [had] to him a creditor, and every man bitter of soul, and he became over them as commander; and were with him about four hundred man.

en.L: And every man in distress, and every man who had a creditor, and every man bitter of soul gathered to him, and he became commander over them. And there were with him about four hundred men.
en.B: Men who were in trouble, men who owed money, and men who were bitter about their lot all came to join him, and he became their commander. There were about four hundred men with him.
en.R: Others came to join him too: men who were in trouble, men who owed money they could not pay, and men who were angry at how life had treated them. David became their commander. About four hundred men were with him.

es.L: Y se juntaron a él todo hombre en apuro, y todo hombre que tenía un acreedor, y todo hombre amargado de alma, y llegó a ser jefe sobre ellos. Y hubo con él unos cuatrocientos hombres.
es.B: Se le unieron hombres que estaban en apuros, hombres que tenían deudas y hombres amargados por su suerte, y él llegó a ser su jefe. Había con él unos cuatrocientos hombres.
es.R: También otros vinieron a unirse a él: hombres que estaban en problemas, hombres que tenían deudas que no podían pagar, y hombres que estaban enojados por cómo los había tratado la vida. David llegó a ser su jefe. Con él había unos cuatrocientos hombres.

fr.L: Et tout homme dans la détresse, et tout homme qui avait un créancier, et tout homme à l’âme amère se rassemblèrent auprès de lui, et il devint leur chef. Et il y eut avec lui environ quatre cents hommes.
fr.B: Des hommes en difficulté, des hommes qui avaient des dettes et des hommes aigris par leur sort vinrent tous le rejoindre, et il devint leur chef. Il y avait avec lui environ quatre cents hommes.
fr.R: D’autres sont venus le rejoindre aussi : des hommes qui avaient des problèmes, des hommes qui avaient des dettes qu’ils ne pouvaient pas payer, et des hommes en colère contre la vie qu’on leur faisait. David est devenu leur chef. Environ quatre cents hommes étaient avec lui.

vi.L: Mọi người đang gặp cảnh khốn cùng, mọi người mắc nợ, và mọi người có linh hồn cay đắng đều tụ họp với ông, và ông trở thành thủ lĩnh của họ. Có khoảng bốn trăm người ở với ông.
vi.B: Những người gặp hoạn nạn, những người mắc nợ, và những người bất mãn đều kéo đến theo ông, và ông trở thành thủ lĩnh của họ. Có khoảng bốn trăm người ở với ông.
vi.R: Có những người khác cũng đến theo ông: những người gặp rắc rối, những người mắc nợ không trả nổi, và những người bực tức vì cuộc đời bất công với họ. Đa-vít trở thành thủ lĩnh của họ. Có khoảng bốn trăm người ở với ông.

decisions.choice: man of distress: someone under pressure or in hard straits
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning to press or squeeze. It covers any kind of hardship, not one particular trouble.

decisions.choice: who had a creditor: a man pressed by someone he owed
decisions.reason: The word names a lender who demands his money back. A debtor who could not pay could lose his land or be sold into service (2 Kings 4:1), so such men had reason to leave home.

decisions.choice: bitter of soul: deeply discontented, hurt or angry
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of Hannah's grief (1:10) and of angry men ready to fight (Judges 18:25). Here it describes men who felt wronged or were unhappy with their lives under Saul.

decisions.choice: commander: the leader of an armed band
decisions.reason: The word is used of officers and chiefs of many kinds. Here David leads a company of fighting men, the band that follows him through the rest of 1 Samuel (23:13; 25:13; 27:2).

decisions.choice: men
decisions.reason: Each item is literally "every man". These are the fighting men of David's band, so men are meant, and no gender setting is used.

decisions.choice: "thủ lĩnh" for the leader of David's band
decisions.reason: The leader of an armed band (m4), not the army's commander, for whom the terms note keeps "tướng chỉ huy quân đội".

source.text: וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ דָּוִ֛ד מִשָּׁ֖ם מִצְפֵּ֣ה מוֹאָ֑ב וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֗ב יֵֽצֵא־נָ֞א אָבִ֤י וְאִמִּי֙ אִתְּכֶ֔ם עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֵדַ֔ע מַה־יַּֽעֲשֶׂה־לִּ֖י אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And went David from there [to] Mizpah of Moab, and said to [the] king of Moab, let go out please my father and my mother with you until that I know what will do for me God.

en.L: And David went from there to Mizpah of Moab, and he said to the king of Moab, "Please let my father and my mother come out [and stay] with you until I know what God will do for me."
en.B: From there David went to Mizpah in Moab and said to the king of Moab, "Please allow my father and mother to come out and stay with you until I know what God will do for me."
en.R: From there David went to Mizpah in the country of Moab. He asked the king of Moab, "Please allow my father and mother to come and live with you until I find out what God is going to do for me."

es.L: Y se fue David de allí a Mizpa de Moab, y dijo al rey de Moab: «Deja, por favor, que mi padre y mi madre salgan [y se queden] con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} hasta que yo sepa lo que Dios hará conmigo».
es.B: De allí David se fue a Mizpa de Moab y le dijo al rey de Moab: «Por favor, permite que mi padre y mi madre vengan a quedarse con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} hasta que yo sepa lo que Dios va a hacer conmigo».
es.R: De allí David se fue a Mizpa, en el país de Moab. Le pidió al rey de Moab: «Por favor, deja que mi padre y mi madre vengan a vivir con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} hasta que yo sepa lo que Dios va a hacer conmigo».

fr.L: Et David alla de là à Mitspa de Moab, et il dit au roi de Moab : « Permets, je te prie, que mon père et ma mère sortent [et restent] avec vous jusqu’à ce que je sache ce que Dieu fera pour moi. »
fr.B: De là, David alla à Mitspa en Moab et dit au roi de Moab : « Permets, je te prie, à mon père et à ma mère de venir s’établir chez vous jusqu’à ce que je sache ce que Dieu va faire pour moi. »
fr.R: De là, David est allé à Mitspa, dans le pays de Moab. Il a demandé au roi de Moab : « S’il te plaît, permets à mon père et à ma mère de venir habiter chez vous jusqu’à ce que je sache ce que Dieu va faire pour moi. »

vi.L: Đa-vít đi từ đó đến Mích-ba ở Mô-áp, và nói với vua Mô-áp: "Xin để cha mẹ tôi ra [ở] với vua, cho đến khi tôi biết Đức Chúa Trời sẽ làm gì cho tôi."
vi.B: Từ đó Đa-vít đi đến Mích-ba ở Mô-áp và nói với vua Mô-áp: "Xin vua cho cha mẹ tôi đến ở với vua cho đến khi tôi biết Đức Chúa Trời sẽ làm gì cho tôi."
vi.R: Từ đó Đa-vít đi đến Mích-ba trong xứ Mô-áp. Ông xin vua Mô-áp: "Xin vua cho cha mẹ tôi đến sống với vua cho đến khi tôi biết Đức Chúa Trời sẽ làm gì cho tôi."

decisions.choice: Mizpah of Moab: a place in Moab whose site is not known
decisions.reason: Mizpah means "lookout" or "watchtower", and several places had the name, including the Mizpah in Benjamin where Samuel gathered Israel (7:5). "Of Moab" marks this one as a different place, east of the Dead Sea.

decisions.choice: the king of Moab: David seeks refuge for his parents with a foreign king
decisions.reason: The text gives no reason why the king of Moab would welcome them. David's great-grandmother Ruth was a Moabite (Ruth 4:13-17), which may explain the link, but the narrator does not say so. Saul had fought Moab (14:47), so its king had no reason to help Saul.

decisions.choice: with you: with the king and his people
decisions.reason: The word "you" is plural. David asks that his parents be allowed to live among the king and his household or people, not with the king alone.

decisions.choice: come out and stay with you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "go out ... with you". Balanced adds "and stay" to make clear that David asks for a place for them to live; Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: "avec vous", "chez vous" (plural)
decisions.reason: The pronoun is plural (m3): the king and his people. French "vous" shows it, while the king himself is "tu" ("Permets").

decisions.choice: con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}
decisions.reason: The Hebrew “with you” is plural: with the king and his people (m3). Spanish shows the plural, so it takes the plural_you span.

source.text: וַיַּנְחֵ֕ם אֶת־פְּנֵ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֑ב וַיֵּשְׁב֣וּ עִמּ֔וֹ כָּל־יְמֵ֥י הֱיוֹת־דָּוִ֖ד בַּמְּצוּדָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he led them [before the] face of [the] king of Moab, and they stayed with him all [the] days of [the] being of David in the stronghold.

en.L: And he led them before the king of Moab, and they stayed with him all the days that David was in the stronghold.
en.B: So he took them to the king of Moab, and they lived with him for as long as David was in the stronghold.
en.R: So David brought his parents to the king of Moab. They lived with him the whole time David was hiding in the stronghold.

es.L: Y los llevó delante del rey de Moab, y se quedaron con él todos los días que David estuvo en la fortaleza.
es.B: Así que los llevó ante el rey de Moab, y ellos vivieron con él todo el tiempo que David estuvo en la fortaleza.
es.R: Así que David llevó a sus padres ante el rey de Moab. Ellos vivieron con él todo el tiempo que David estuvo escondido en la fortaleza.

fr.L: Et il les conduisit devant le roi de Moab, et ils demeurèrent avec lui tout le temps que David fut dans la forteresse.
fr.B: Il les conduisit donc auprès du roi de Moab, et ils restèrent chez lui tout le temps que David fut dans la forteresse.
fr.R: David a donc conduit ses parents chez le roi de Moab. Ils ont habité chez lui pendant tout le temps où David se cachait dans la forteresse.

vi.L: Ông dẫn họ đến trước mặt vua Mô-áp, và họ ở với vua suốt những ngày Đa-vít ở trong đồn.
vi.B: Vậy ông đưa cha mẹ đến với vua Mô-áp, và họ sống với vua suốt thời gian Đa-vít ở trong đồn.
vi.R: Vậy Đa-vít đưa cha mẹ đến với vua Mô-áp. Họ sống với vua suốt thời gian Đa-vít ẩn náu trong đồn.

decisions.choice: he led them: David brought his parents to the king
alternatives: he left them with the king of Moab
decisions.reason: The vowels of the text give a verb meaning "lead" or "guide". With different vowels the same letters would mean "he left them". Either way David put his parents in the care of the king of Moab.

decisions.choice: the stronghold: a hard-to-reach place of refuge, perhaps in Moab
decisions.reason: The word means a fortified height or a natural refuge. Which stronghold is meant is not said. Because the prophet tells David in verse 5 to leave it and go into the land of Judah, it seems to lie outside Judah, near Moab, rather than at Adullam.

decisions.choice: David ... his parents ... hiding
decisions.reason: Readable names who led whom, and says "hiding" because the stronghold was a refuge from Saul.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ גָּ֨ד הַנָּבִ֜יא אֶל־דָּוִ֗ד לֹ֤א תֵשֵׁב֙ בַּמְּצוּדָ֔ה לֵ֥ךְ וּבָֽאתָ־לְּךָ֖ אֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֔ד וַיָּבֹ֖א יַ֥עַר חָֽרֶת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said Gad the prophet to David, not you shall stay in the stronghold; go, and you shall go for yourself [to the] land of Judah. And went David and came [to the] forest of Hereth.

en.L: And Gad the prophet said to David, "Do not stay in the stronghold. Go, and enter the land of Judah." And David went and came to the forest of Hereth.
en.B: Then Gad the prophet told David, "Do not remain in the stronghold. Leave, and go into the land of Judah." So David left and came to the forest of Hereth.
en.R: Then the prophet Gad told David, "Do not stay in the stronghold. Leave it and go to the land of Judah." David left and went into the forest of Hereth.

es.L: Y dijo el profeta Gad a David: «No te quedes en la fortaleza. Vete, y entra en la tierra de Judá». Y se fue David y llegó al bosque de Haret.
es.B: Entonces el profeta Gad le dijo a David: «No te quedes en la fortaleza. Sal de ahí y vete a la tierra de Judá». Así que David se fue y llegó al bosque de Haret.
es.R: Entonces el profeta Gad le dijo a David: «No te quedes en la fortaleza. Sal de ahí y vete a la tierra de Judá». David se fue y entró en el bosque de Haret.

fr.L: Et Gad le prophète dit à David : « Ne reste pas dans la forteresse. Va, et entre dans le pays de Juda. » Et David s’en alla et vint dans la forêt de Hèreth.
fr.B: Alors le prophète Gad dit à David : « Ne reste pas dans la forteresse. Pars et va dans le pays de Juda. » David partit donc et arriva dans la forêt de Hèreth.
fr.R: Ensuite, le prophète Gad a dit à David : « Ne reste pas dans la forteresse. Pars et va dans le pays de Juda. » David est parti et il est allé dans la forêt de Hèreth.

vi.L: Nhà tiên tri Gát nói với Đa-vít: "Đừng ở trong đồn nữa. Hãy đi, vào xứ Giu-đa." Đa-vít đi và đến rừng Hê-rết.
vi.B: Bấy giờ nhà tiên tri Gát bảo Đa-vít: "Đừng ở lại trong đồn. Hãy rời khỏi đây mà vào xứ Giu-đa." Vậy Đa-vít ra đi và đến rừng Hê-rết.
vi.R: Bấy giờ nhà tiên tri Gát bảo Đa-vít: "Đừng ở trong đồn nữa. Hãy rời khỏi đó và đi về xứ Giu-đa." Đa-vít ra đi và vào rừng Hê-rết.

decisions.choice: Gad the prophet: a prophet who guides David
decisions.reason: This is Gad's first appearance. Later he is called David's seer and brings him the LORD's word (2 Samuel 24:11-19). His word here shows that God is guiding David even while he is a fugitive.

decisions.choice: do not stay: a firm instruction
decisions.reason: The negative with the plain future form is a strong command, as in "you shall not". David obeys at once.

decisions.choice: the forest of Hereth: a wooded area in Judah whose site is not known
decisions.reason: The name appears only here. The hills of Judah were more wooded then than they are now.

decisions.choice: "nhà tiên tri Gát"; "rừng Hê-rết"
alternatives: "Gát" for the prophet spelled apart from the city
decisions.reason: The prophet's name takes the same form as Gad son of Jacob in the Vietnamese Genesis; it matches the city of Gath in Vietnamese, so the prophet is always named with his title.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע שָׁא֔וּל כִּ֚י נוֹדַ֣ע דָּוִ֔ד וַאֲנָשִׁ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֑וֹ וְשָׁאוּל֩ יוֹשֵׁ֨ב בַּגִּבְעָ֜ה תַּֽחַת־הָאֶ֤שֶׁל בָּֽרָמָה֙ וַחֲנִית֣וֹ בְיָד֔וֹ וְכָל־עֲבָדָ֖יו נִצָּבִ֥ים עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard Saul that was known David and [the] men who [were] with him; and Saul [was] sitting in Gibeah under the tamarisk on the height, and his spear [was] in his hand, and all his servants [were] standing by him.

en.L: And Saul heard that David and the men who [were] with him had been discovered. And Saul [was] sitting in Gibeah under the tamarisk on the height, and his spear [was] in his hand, and all his servants [were] standing by him.
en.B: Saul heard that David and the men with him had been found. Saul was sitting in Gibeah under the tamarisk tree on the height, with his spear in his hand, and all his officials were standing around him.
en.R: Saul heard that people knew where David and his men were. At the time Saul was sitting in Gibeah under the tamarisk tree on the hill. He had his spear in his hand, and all his officials were standing around him.

es.L: Y oyó Saúl que se había descubierto a David y a los hombres que [estaban] con él. Y Saúl [estaba] sentado en Guibeá, bajo el tamarisco en la altura, y su lanza [estaba] en su mano, y todos sus siervos [estaban] de pie junto a él.
es.B: Saúl se enteró de que habían descubierto a David y a los hombres que estaban con él. Saúl estaba sentado en Guibeá, bajo el tamarisco de la colina, con la lanza en la mano, y todos sus oficiales estaban de pie a su alrededor.
es.R: Saúl oyó que la gente sabía dónde estaban David y sus hombres. En ese momento Saúl estaba sentado en Guibeá, bajo el tamarisco de la colina. Tenía la lanza en la mano, y todos sus oficiales estaban de pie a su alrededor.

fr.L: Et Saül apprit que David et les hommes qui [étaient] avec lui avaient été découverts. Et Saül [était] assis à Guibea sous le tamaris, sur la hauteur, sa lance à la main, et tous ses serviteurs [se tenaient] près de lui.
fr.B: Saül apprit qu’on avait découvert David et les hommes qui étaient avec lui. Saül était assis à Guibea, sous le tamaris de la hauteur, sa lance à la main, et tous ses officiers se tenaient autour de lui.
fr.R: Saül a appris que des gens savaient où étaient David et ses hommes. À ce moment-là, Saül était assis à Guibea, sous le tamaris, sur la colline. Il avait sa lance à la main, et tous ses officiers étaient debout autour de lui.

vi.L: Sau-lơ nghe rằng người ta đã biết được Đa-vít và những người ở với ông. Sau-lơ đang ngồi tại Ghi-bê-a, dưới cây thánh liễu trên nơi cao, tay cầm giáo, và tất cả các đầy tớ của ông đứng quanh ông.
vi.B: Sau-lơ nghe tin người ta đã tìm ra Đa-vít và những người theo ông. Lúc ấy Sau-lơ đang ngồi tại Ghi-bê-a, dưới cây thánh liễu trên đồi cao, tay cầm giáo, và tất cả quần thần đứng chung quanh.
vi.R: Sau-lơ nghe tin người ta biết Đa-vít và thuộc hạ đang ở đâu. Lúc ấy Sau-lơ đang ngồi tại Ghi-bê-a, dưới cây thánh liễu trên đồi. Vua cầm cây giáo trong tay, và tất cả quần thần đứng chung quanh.

decisions.choice: was known: their whereabouts had become known
decisions.reason: The verb means "was made known" or "was discovered". Saul learns where David and his band are.

decisions.choice: on the height: a hill or high place in Gibeah, not the town of Ramah
decisions.reason: The word has the article, "the height", and Saul is said to be in Gibeah, his home town (10:26). So it names a raised place in Gibeah rather than Samuel's town Ramah.

decisions.choice: under the tamarisk, spear in hand: Saul holding court
decisions.reason: A ruler often sat under a large tree to meet his people (14:2; Judges 4:5). Saul's spear is the mark of his royal power, and also the weapon he has already thrown at David and Jonathan (18:10-11; 19:9-10; 20:33).

decisions.choice: his officials (Balanced, Readable); his servants (Literal)
decisions.reason: The men standing around the king are his courtiers and officers. Literal keeps "servants"; Balanced and Readable say "officials", as for the king's servants elsewhere in Samuel.

decisions.choice: "cây thánh liễu" for the tamarisk
decisions.reason: As the Vietnamese Genesis 21:33.

en.B: Saul said to the officials standing around him, "Listen, you men of Benjamin! Will the son of Jesse give fields and vineyards to every one of you too? Will he make all of you commanders over thousands and over hundreds?

fr.B: Saül dit aux officiers qui se tenaient autour de lui : « Écoutez, hommes de Benjamin ! Le fils de Jessé vous donnera-t-il, à vous tous aussi, des champs et des vignes ? Fera-t-il de vous tous des chefs de milliers et des chefs de centaines ?
fr.R: Saül a dit aux officiers qui étaient autour de lui : « Écoutez-moi, hommes de la tribu de Benjamin ! Vous croyez que le fils de Jessé va vous donner à tous des champs et des vignes ? Est-ce qu’il va faire de chacun de vous le chef de mille soldats ou de cent soldats ?

vi.L: Sau-lơ nói với các đầy tớ đang đứng quanh mình: "Hãy nghe đây, hỡi con cháu Bên-gia-min! Con trai Gie-sê cũng sẽ cho tất cả các ngươi ruộng đất và vườn nho sao? Nó sẽ lập tất cả các ngươi làm chỉ huy ngàn người và chỉ huy trăm người sao?

vi.R: Sau-lơ nói với quần thần đang đứng chung quanh: "Hãy nghe ta, hỡi người thuộc chi tộc Bên-gia-min! Các ngươi tưởng con trai Gie-sê sẽ cho tất cả các ngươi ruộng đất và vườn nho sao? Nó sẽ cho mỗi người các ngươi chỉ huy một ngàn hay một trăm quân lính sao?

decisions.choice: sons of Benjamin: Saul's own tribe
decisions.reason: Saul was a Benjaminite (9:1-2), and his court was made up of his own tribesmen. David is from Judah. Saul appeals to tribal loyalty: they owe what they have to a king from their own tribe.

decisions.choice: the son of Jesse: a scornful way to refer to David
decisions.reason: Saul avoids saying David's name and names him by his father, a farmer of Bethlehem, as he did in 20:27-31.

decisions.choice: two questions expecting the answer "no"
decisions.reason: "Also" means "as I have done". Saul is reminding his men that he has rewarded them with land and rank, and that David will not do the same for Benjaminites.

decisions.choice: commanders of thousands and of hundreds: officers in the king's army
decisions.reason: These were the ranks a king gave to his loyal men, along with fields and vineyards, just as Samuel had warned that a king would do (8:12, 14).

decisions.choice: men of Benjamin
decisions.reason: "Sons of Benjamin" means members of the tribe. The men Saul speaks to are his officers, so Balanced and Readable say "men of Benjamin" without a gender setting.

decisions.choice: hijos de Benjamín (L); hombres de Benjamín (B, R)
decisions.reason: Saul appeals to his own tribe (m1). Literal keeps the Hebrew “sons”; Balanced and Readable say “hombres”, as the English “men of Benjamin” (r-en-1).

records.literal_gloss: For you have conspired all of you against me, and there is none uncovering my ear when cuts my son [a covenant] with [the] son of Jesse, and there is none of you sick for me or uncovering my ear that has raised up my son my servant against me as an ambusher as this day.

en.L: For all of you have conspired against me, and there is no one who uncovers my ear when my son cuts [a covenant] with the son of Jesse, and there is no one of you who is sorry for me or uncovers my ear that my son has stirred up my servant against me to lie in wait, as [it is] this day."
en.B: All of you have plotted against me! No one told me when my son made a covenant with the son of Jesse. None of you feels sorry for me or lets me know that my son has stirred up my servant to lie in wait against me, as he is doing today."
en.R: You have all plotted against me! Nobody told me when my son Jonathan made a covenant with the son of Jesse. Nobody here cares about me. Nobody warned me that my own son has turned my servant against me. Now that servant is waiting in hiding to attack me, as you can see today."

es.L: Porque todos {{plural_you:ustedes han conspirado|vosotros habéis conspirado}} contra mí, y no hay quien descubra mi oído cuando mi hijo corta [pacto] con el hijo de Isaí, y no hay ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que se duela por mí o que descubra mi oído de que mi hijo ha levantado contra mí a mi siervo para que me aceche, como [sucede] este día».
es.B: ¡Todos {{plural_you:ustedes han conspirado|vosotros habéis conspirado}} contra mí! Nadie me avisó cuando mi hijo hizo un pacto con el hijo de Isaí. Ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} siente pena por mí ni me hace saber que mi hijo ha incitado a mi siervo a acecharme, como lo está haciendo hoy».
es.R: ¡Todos {{plural_you:ustedes han hecho planes|vosotros habéis hecho planes}} contra mí! Nadie me dijo nada cuando mi hijo Jonatán hizo un pacto con el hijo de Isaí. A nadie aquí le importo. Nadie me advirtió que mi propio hijo ha puesto a mi siervo en contra mía. Ahora ese siervo está escondido esperando para atacarme, como {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} ver hoy».

fr.L: Car vous avez tous conspiré contre moi, et il n’y a personne qui m’ait découvert l’oreille quand mon fils a conclu [une alliance] avec le fils de Jessé, et il n’y a personne parmi vous qui ait mal pour moi et qui m’ait découvert l’oreille que mon fils a soulevé mon serviteur contre moi pour me dresser des embûches, comme [c’est le cas] aujourd’hui. »
fr.B: Vous avez tous comploté contre moi ! Personne ne m’a averti quand mon fils a conclu une alliance avec le fils de Jessé. Aucun de vous ne se soucie de moi ni ne m’a fait savoir que mon fils a dressé mon serviteur contre moi pour me tendre un piège, comme il le fait aujourd’hui. »
fr.R: Vous avez tous comploté contre moi ! Personne ne m’a dit que mon fils Jonathan avait fait une alliance avec le fils de Jessé. Personne ici ne s’inquiète pour moi. Personne ne m’a prévenu que mon propre fils a dressé mon serviteur contre moi. Maintenant, ce serviteur se cache pour m’attaquer, vous le voyez bien aujourd’hui. »

vi.L: Vì tất cả các ngươi đã âm mưu chống lại ta, và không có ai mở tai cho ta khi con trai ta kết [giao ước] với con trai Gie-sê; không ai trong các ngươi xót thương ta hay mở tai cho ta rằng con trai ta đã xúi đầy tớ của ta nổi lên chống lại ta để rình phục, như ngày nay."
vi.B: Tất cả các ngươi đã âm mưu chống lại ta! Không ai báo cho ta biết khi con trai ta lập giao ước với con trai Gie-sê. Không ai trong các ngươi thương xót ta hay cho ta biết rằng con trai ta đã xúi giục đầy tớ của ta rình rập hại ta, như nó đang làm hôm nay."
vi.R: Tất cả các ngươi đã âm mưu chống lại ta! Không ai nói cho ta biết khi con trai ta là Giô-na-than lập giao ước với con trai Gie-sê. Ở đây không ai quan tâm đến ta. Không ai báo cho ta biết rằng chính con trai ta đã xúi đầy tớ của ta chống lại ta. Bây giờ đầy tớ ấy đang rình rập để tấn công ta, như các ngươi thấy hôm nay."

decisions.choice: for you have conspired: the charge that explains Saul's questions
decisions.reason: The opening word links this verse to the questions of verse 7: Saul asks them why they would favor David, since they are acting as if they are in league with him. The verb is used of a plot against a king (2 Samuel 15:31; 2 Kings 10:9).

decisions.choice: uncover my ear: tell me, let me know
decisions.reason: The picture is of moving the hair or headcloth aside to speak into someone's ear. Jonathan used the same phrase when he promised to tell David what he learned (20:2, 12-13).

decisions.choice: cuts: makes a covenant
decisions.reason: "Cut" with no object is short for "cut a covenant", the usual Hebrew phrase for making a covenant. Saul means the covenant between Jonathan and David (18:3; 20:16).

decisions.choice: sick for me: grieved on my behalf, concerned for me
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "be sick". Here it describes feeling pain for someone else, being troubled over what is happening to him.

decisions.choice: my servant ... to lie in wait: Saul's charge is false
decisions.reason: Saul accuses Jonathan of stirring up David to ambush him. Nothing in the story supports it: David has only fled, and later he spares Saul's life when he could have killed him (24:5-8; 26:8-11).

decisions.choice: my son Jonathan
decisions.reason: Readable names the son Saul means, and splits the long accusation into short sentences.

en.B: Then Doeg the Edomite, who was standing with Saul's officials, spoke up: "I saw the son of Jesse come to Nob, to Ahimelech son of Ahitub.
en.R: Doeg, the man from Edom, was standing there with Saul's officials. He said, "I saw the son of Jesse when he came to Ahimelech son of Ahitub at Nob.

es.B: Entonces Doeg el edomita, que estaba con los oficiales de Saúl, tomó la palabra: «Yo vi al hijo de Isaí llegar a Nob, a casa de Ahimelec hijo de Ahitob.
es.R: Doeg, el hombre de Edom, estaba allí con los oficiales de Saúl. Dijo: «Yo vi al hijo de Isaí cuando fue a ver a Ahimelec hijo de Ahitob, en Nob.

fr.L: Et Doëg l’Édomite, qui se tenait près des serviteurs de Saül, répondit et dit : « J’ai vu le fils de Jessé venir à Nob, chez Ahimélek, fils d’Ahitoub.
fr.B: Alors Doëg l’Édomite, qui se tenait parmi les officiers de Saül, prit la parole : « J’ai vu le fils de Jessé venir à Nob, chez Ahimélek, fils d’Ahitoub.
fr.R: Doëg, l’homme d’Édom, était là avec les officiers de Saül. Il a dit : « J’ai vu le fils de Jessé quand il est venu chez Ahimélek, fils d’Ahitoub, à Nob.

vi.L: Đô-e người Ê-đôm, đang đứng cạnh các đầy tớ của Sau-lơ, trả lời: "Tôi đã thấy con trai Gie-sê đến Nóp, đến với A-hi-mê-léc con trai A-hi-túp.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Đô-e người Ê-đôm, đang đứng với các quần thần của Sau-lơ, lên tiếng: "Tôi đã thấy con trai Gie-sê đến Nóp, gặp A-hi-mê-léc con trai A-hi-túp.
vi.R: Đô-e, người Ê-đôm, đang đứng đó với các quần thần của Sau-lơ. Ông ta nói: "Tôi đã thấy con trai Gie-sê khi nó đến gặp A-hi-mê-léc con trai A-hi-túp tại Nóp.

decisions.choice: standing by Saul's servants: standing among or beside them
alternatives: who was set over Saul's servants
decisions.reason: The preposition usually means "over" or "by". Here it most likely means he stood with them. Some take it as "in charge of" Saul's servants, since Doeg was a senior man (21:8), but in this scene everyone is simply standing before the king.

decisions.choice: Doeg the Edomite: the man David saw at Nob
decisions.reason: Doeg was the chief of Saul's shepherds and was held at the sanctuary at Nob on the day David came (21:8). Now he answers Saul's complaint that no one tells him anything.

decisions.choice: the son of Jesse: Doeg speaks of David in Saul's own scornful way
decisions.reason: Doeg uses the same phrase Saul has just used (verses 7-8), showing that he is siding with the king.

decisions.choice: Saul's officials
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, the king's servants are his courtiers.

decisions.choice: Doeg el edomita; Ahitob
decisions.reason: Doeg as the Samuel terms note has him (m2); Ahitub takes its usual Spanish form, “Ahitob”, and keeps it wherever he is named.

vi.R: A-hi-mê-léc đã cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xem Đa-vít nên làm gì. Ông ấy cũng cho Đa-vít thức ăn và gươm của Gô-li-át người Phi-li-tin."

decisions.choice: inquired of Yahweh for him: asked God's guidance on David's behalf
decisions.reason: A priest could ask God for a decision, often with the ephod or the Urim and Thummim (14:36-42; 23:9-12). Doeg says that Ahimelech did this for David.

decisions.choice: the inquiry: not mentioned in the account of chapter 21
decisions.reason: Chapter 21 tells of the bread and the sword but says nothing about an inquiry. Ahimelech's answer in verse 15 implies that he had asked God for David before as a matter of course. Doeg's report is told from his own angle, and the narrator does not say whether he adds this detail or whether chapter 21 simply leaves it out.

decisions.choice: provisions ... the sword: placed first for emphasis
decisions.reason: Both objects come before their verbs, stressing what Ahimelech handed over: food for the road and a weapon.

decisions.choice: Ahimelech ... David
decisions.reason: Readable names the priest and David where the Hebrew says "he" and "him".

decisions.choice: consulter le SEIGNEUR
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for "inquire of the LORD"; Readable says what was asked, as the English.

decisions.choice: consultar al SEÑOR
decisions.reason: The Samuel terms note's wording for inquiring of the LORD, asking God's guidance (m1); Readable says it plainly with “preguntar”. Recorded once for this block.

decisions.choice: "cầu hỏi CHÚA"
decisions.reason: The Samuel terms note's phrase for inquiring of the LORD; it is used the same way through the block.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ לִקְרֹא֩ אֶת־אֲחִימֶ֨לֶךְ בֶּן־אֲחִיט֜וּב הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־בֵּ֥ית אָבִ֛יו הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּנֹ֑ב וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ כֻלָּ֖ם אֶל־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And sent the king to call Ahimelech son of Ahitub the priest and all [the] house of his father, the priests who [were] in Nob; and came all of them to the king.

en.L: And the king sent to summon Ahimelech son of Ahitub, the priest, and all his father's house, the priests who [were] in Nob, and all of them came to the king.
en.B: The king sent for Ahimelech the priest, son of Ahitub, and for all his father's family, the priests at Nob, and they all came to the king.
en.R: So the king sent for Ahimelech the priest, son of Ahitub, and for all his relatives, who were the priests at Nob. They all came to the king.

es.L: Y envió el rey a llamar a Ahimelec hijo de Ahitob, el sacerdote, y a toda la casa de su padre, los sacerdotes que [estaban] en Nob; y vinieron todos ellos al rey.
es.B: El rey mandó llamar al sacerdote Ahimelec hijo de Ahitob, y a toda la familia de su padre, los sacerdotes de Nob, y todos vinieron ante el rey.
es.R: Entonces el rey mandó llamar al sacerdote Ahimelec hijo de Ahitob, y a todos sus parientes, que eran los sacerdotes de Nob. Todos vinieron ante el rey.

fr.L: Et le roi envoya appeler Ahimélek, fils d’Ahitoub, le prêtre, et toute la maison de son père, les prêtres qui [étaient] à Nob ; et ils vinrent tous chez le roi.
fr.B: Le roi fit appeler le prêtre Ahimélek, fils d’Ahitoub, et toute la famille de son père, les prêtres de Nob, et ils vinrent tous chez le roi.
fr.R: Alors le roi a fait venir Ahimélek le prêtre, fils d’Ahitoub, et toute sa famille, qui étaient les prêtres de Nob. Ils sont tous venus chez le roi.

vi.L: Vua sai người gọi thầy tế lễ A-hi-mê-léc con trai A-hi-túp, cùng cả nhà cha ông, là các thầy tế lễ ở Nóp, và tất cả họ đều đến với vua.
vi.B: Vua cho đòi thầy tế lễ A-hi-mê-léc con trai A-hi-túp, cùng cả gia đình cha ông, là các thầy tế lễ ở Nóp, và tất cả họ đều đến với vua.
vi.R: Vua cho gọi thầy tế lễ A-hi-mê-léc con trai A-hi-túp, cùng tất cả bà con của ông, là các thầy tế lễ ở Nóp. Tất cả họ đều đến gặp vua.

decisions.choice: all his father's house, the priests: the priestly family descended from Eli
decisions.reason: Ahimelech's father Ahitub was a grandson of Eli (14:3). The whole family served as priests at Nob after Shiloh was lost (21:2).

decisions.choice: the house of Eli summoned to the king
decisions.reason: A man of God had told Eli that his family would be cut down and few would reach old age (2:31-33; 3:12-14). The slaughter that follows is part of that word coming true.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֔וּל שְֽׁמַֽע־נָ֖א בֶּן־אֲחִיט֑וּב וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנְנִ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Saul, hear please, son of Ahitub. And he said, here I [am], my lord.

en.L: And Saul said, "Hear now, son of Ahitub." And he said, "Here I am, my lord."
en.B: Saul said, "Listen now, son of Ahitub." He answered, "Yes, my lord."
en.R: Saul said, "Listen to me, son of Ahitub." Ahimelech answered, "Yes, my lord, I am listening."

es.L: Y dijo Saúl: «Oye ahora, hijo de Ahitob». Y él dijo: «Heme aquí, señor mío».
es.B: Saúl le dijo: «Escucha, hijo de Ahitob». Él respondió: «Sí, mi señor».
es.R: Saúl le dijo: «Escúchame, hijo de Ahitob». Ahimelec le contestó: «Sí, mi señor, te escucho».

fr.L: Et Saül dit : « Écoute donc, fils d’Ahitoub. » Et il dit : « Me voici, mon seigneur. »
fr.B: Saül dit : « Écoute-moi, fils d’Ahitoub. » Il répondit : « Oui, mon seigneur. »
fr.R: Saül a dit : « Écoute-moi, fils d’Ahitoub. » Ahimélek a répondu : « Oui, mon seigneur, je t’écoute. »

vi.L: Sau-lơ nói: "Hãy nghe đây, hỡi con trai A-hi-túp." Ông đáp: "Thưa chúa tôi, có tôi đây."
vi.B: Sau-lơ nói: "Con trai A-hi-túp, hãy nghe đây." Ông đáp: "Thưa bệ hạ, có tôi."
vi.R: Sau-lơ nói: "Hãy nghe ta, hỡi con trai A-hi-túp." A-hi-mê-léc đáp: "Thưa đức vua, tôi đang nghe."

decisions.choice: son of Ahitub: addressing Ahimelech by his father's name
decisions.reason: Saul does not use the priest's name, just as he speaks of David as "the son of Jesse". It is cold and distant.

decisions.choice: here I am: I am ready to listen
decisions.reason: The word is the usual answer of someone who is called and is at the speaker's service (3:4-8).

decisions.choice: Yes, my lord (Balanced); Yes, my lord, I am listening (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Here I am" is a reply to being called, not a statement of where someone is. Balanced and Readable use a natural English answer.

decisions.choice: "my lord" to the king: "chúa tôi" (L), "bệ hạ" (B), "đức vua" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note for "my lord the king"; this holds through the block.

records.literal_gloss: And said to him Saul, why have you conspired against me, you and [the] son of Jesse, in your giving to him bread and a sword and inquiring for him of God, to rise against me as an ambusher as this day?

en.L: And Saul said to him, "Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, by your giving him bread and a sword and inquiring of God for him, so that he has risen against me to lie in wait, as [it is] this day?"
en.B: Saul said to him, "Why have you and the son of Jesse plotted against me? You gave him bread and a sword and asked God for guidance for him, so that he could rise up against me and lie in wait, as he is doing today."
en.R: Saul said to him, "Why have you and the son of Jesse made plans against me? You gave him food and a sword. You asked God what he should do. Now he has turned against me and is waiting in hiding to attack me, as you can see today."

es.L: Y le dijo Saúl: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:han conspirado|habéis conspirado}} contra mí, tú y el hijo de Isaí, al darle tú pan y espada y consultar por él a Dios, para que se levante contra mí y me aceche, como [sucede] este día?».
es.B: Saúl le dijo: «¿Por qué tú y el hijo de Isaí {{plural_you:han conspirado|habéis conspirado}} contra mí? Le diste pan y una espada y consultaste a Dios por él, para que se levantara contra mí y me acechara, como lo está haciendo hoy».
es.R: Saúl le dijo: «¿Por qué tú y el hijo de Isaí {{plural_you:han hecho|habéis hecho}} planes contra mí? Le diste comida y una espada. Le preguntaste a Dios lo que él debía hacer. Ahora se ha puesto en contra mía y está escondido esperando para atacarme, como puedes ver hoy».

fr.L: Et Saül lui dit : « Pourquoi avez-vous conspiré contre moi, toi et le fils de Jessé, en lui donnant du pain et une épée et en consultant Dieu pour lui, pour qu’il se dresse contre moi et me tende des embûches, comme [c’est le cas] aujourd’hui ? »
fr.B: Saül lui dit : « Pourquoi avez-vous comploté contre moi, toi et le fils de Jessé ? Tu lui as donné du pain et une épée, et tu as consulté Dieu pour lui, pour qu’il se dresse contre moi et me tende un piège, comme il le fait aujourd’hui. »
fr.R: Saül lui a dit : « Pourquoi est-ce que toi et le fils de Jessé, vous avez préparé un complot contre moi ? Tu lui as donné de la nourriture et une épée. Tu as demandé à Dieu ce qu’il devait faire. Maintenant, il s’est révolté contre moi et il se cache pour m’attaquer, tu le vois bien aujourd’hui. »

vi.L: Sau-lơ nói với ông: "Tại sao ngươi và con trai Gie-sê âm mưu chống lại ta, khi ngươi cho nó bánh và gươm, và cầu hỏi Đức Chúa Trời cho nó, để nó nổi lên chống lại ta mà rình phục, như ngày nay?"
vi.B: Sau-lơ nói với ông: "Tại sao ngươi và con trai Gie-sê âm mưu chống lại ta? Ngươi đã cho nó bánh và gươm, lại cầu hỏi Đức Chúa Trời cho nó, để nó nổi lên rình rập hại ta, như nó đang làm hôm nay."
vi.R: Sau-lơ nói với ông: "Tại sao ngươi và con trai Gie-sê bày mưu chống lại ta? Ngươi đã cho nó thức ăn và gươm. Ngươi đã cầu hỏi Đức Chúa Trời xem nó nên làm gì. Bây giờ nó đã quay lại chống ta và đang rình rập để tấn công ta, như ngươi thấy hôm nay."

decisions.choice: you and the son of Jesse: both charged together
decisions.reason: The verb is plural, "you have conspired", and its subjects are Ahimelech and David. Saul treats the priest's help as part of a plot.

decisions.choice: giving ... inquiring ... to rise: the deeds and their result
decisions.reason: The help (bread, sword, inquiry) is the evidence of the plot, and "to rise against me" gives its outcome or purpose. Saul repeats his charge from verse 8 that David lies in wait for him.

decisions.choice: to lie in wait
decisions.reason: "As an ambusher" is put as "to lie in wait", as in verse 8.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:han conspirado|habéis conspirado}} with “tú y el hijo de Isaí”
decisions.reason: Saul speaks to Ahimelech but charges him and David together (m1); the subject “you and the son of Jesse” is a second person plural, so the verb takes the plural_you span.

source.text: וַיַּ֧עַן אֲחִימֶ֛לֶךְ אֶת־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר וּמִ֤י בְכָל־עֲבָדֶ֨יךָ֙ כְּדָוִ֣ד נֶאֱמָ֔ן וַחֲתַ֥ן הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְסָ֥ר אֶל־מִשְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ךָ וְנִכְבָּ֥ד בְּבֵיתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered Ahimelech the king and said, and who among all your servants [is] like David, faithful, and son-in-law of the king, and turning aside to your bodyguard, and honored in your house?

en.L: And Ahimelech answered the king and said, "And who among all your servants [is] as faithful as David, the king's son-in-law, who turns aside to your bodyguard, and [is] honored in your house?
en.B: Ahimelech answered the king, "Who among all your officials is as faithful as David? He is the king's son-in-law, he has a place in your personal guard, and he is honored in your household.
en.R: Ahimelech answered the king, "None of your officials is as loyal to you as David! He is married to your daughter. He is one of your own bodyguards, and everyone in your palace respects him.

es.L: Y respondió Ahimelec al rey y dijo: «¿Y quién entre todos tus siervos [es] tan fiel como David, yerno del rey, que tiene acceso a tu guardia personal y [es] honrado en tu casa?
es.B: Ahimelec le respondió al rey: «¿Quién de todos tus oficiales es tan fiel como David? Es el yerno del rey, tiene un puesto en tu guardia personal y es honrado en tu casa.
es.R: Ahimelec le contestó al rey: «¡Ninguno de tus oficiales te es tan leal como David! Está casado con tu hija. Es uno de tus propios guardaespaldas, y todos en tu palacio lo respetan.

fr.L: Et Ahimélek répondit au roi et dit : « Et qui, parmi tous tes serviteurs, [est] aussi fidèle que David, le gendre du roi, qui a accès à ta garde personnelle et [qui est] honoré dans ta maison ?
fr.B: Ahimélek répondit au roi : « Lequel de tous tes officiers est aussi fidèle que David ? Il est le gendre du roi, il fait partie de ta garde personnelle et il est honoré dans ta maison.
fr.R: Ahimélek a répondu au roi : « Aucun de tes officiers ne t’est aussi fidèle que David ! Il est marié avec ta fille. Il fait partie de tes gardes du corps, et tout le monde le respecte dans ton palais.

vi.L: A-hi-mê-léc trả lời vua: "Trong tất cả các đầy tớ của vua, có ai trung tín như Đa-vít, là con rể của vua, người được vào đội cận vệ của vua, và được tôn trọng trong nhà vua?
vi.B: A-hi-mê-léc thưa với vua: "Trong tất cả quần thần của bệ hạ, có ai trung thành như Đa-vít? Ông ấy là con rể của bệ hạ, có chỗ trong đội cận vệ của bệ hạ, và được kính trọng trong hoàng gia.
vi.R: A-hi-mê-léc thưa với vua: "Trong tất cả quần thần của đức vua, không ai trung thành với vua bằng Đa-vít! Ông ấy là con rể của vua. Ông ấy là một trong những người cận vệ của vua, và mọi người trong cung đều kính trọng ông ấy.

decisions.choice: faithful: trustworthy, reliable
decisions.reason: The word describes someone who can be relied on, the opposite of the traitor Saul thinks David is. The same word is used of Samuel as a trustworthy prophet (3:20).

decisions.choice: turns aside to your bodyguard: has access to the king's guard or inner circle
decisions.reason: As the text is pointed, the first word is a verb, "turns aside to", that is, joins or has free access to the king's guard. The ancient Greek translation reads the same letters as a noun, "commander of", giving "commander of your bodyguard". David had been set over Saul's fighting men (18:5, 13), so both make sense.

decisions.choice: the king's son-in-law
decisions.reason: David had married Saul's daughter Michal (18:27), so he belonged to the royal family.

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer "no one"
decisions.reason: Ahimelech asks who is as faithful as David, meaning that no one is.

decisions.choice: None of your officials is as loyal to you as David! He is married to your daughter.
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies and explains "son-in-law". "Loyal" gives the sense of the word for faithful in this setting.

decisions.choice: your officials
decisions.reason: The king's servants are his courtiers, as in verse 6.

source.text: הַיּ֧וֹם הַחִלֹּ֛תִי לִשְׁאָל־ל֥וֹ בֵאלֹהִ֖ים חָלִ֣ילָה לִּ֑י אַל־יָשֵׂם֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ בְּעַבְדּ֤וֹ דָבָר֙ בְּכָל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔י כִּ֠י לֹֽא־יָדַ֤ע עַבְדְּךָ֙ בְּכָל־זֹ֔את דָּבָ֥ר קָטֹ֖ן א֥וֹ גָדֽוֹל׃

records.literal_gloss: Today did I begin to inquire for him of God? Far be it from me! Let not put the king against his servant a thing, against all [the] house of my father, for not knew your servant in all this a thing small or great.

en.L: Did I begin today to inquire of God for him? Far be it from me! Let the king not lay anything against his servant [or] against all my father's house, for your servant knew nothing of all this, small or great."
en.B: Was today the first time I asked God for guidance for him? Far be it from me! Let the king not charge his servant or any of my father's family with anything, for your servant knew nothing at all about this, small or great."
en.R: This was not the first time I asked God to guide David. I would never plot against you! Please, my king, do not blame me or any of my family. I did not know anything at all about this."

es.L: ¿Acaso hoy comencé a consultar a Dios por él? ¡Lejos esté de mí! Que no impute el rey cosa alguna a su siervo [ni] a toda la casa de mi padre, porque tu siervo no sabía nada de todo esto, ni poco ni mucho».
es.B: ¿Era hoy la primera vez que consultaba a Dios por él? ¡De ninguna manera! Que el rey no acuse de nada a su siervo ni a nadie de la familia de mi padre, porque tu siervo no sabía absolutamente nada de esto».
es.R: No era la primera vez que le preguntaba a Dios por David. ¡Yo nunca conspiraría contra ti! Por favor, rey mío, no me culpes a mí ni a nadie de mi familia. Yo no sabía nada de todo esto».

fr.L: Est-ce aujourd’hui que j’ai commencé à consulter Dieu pour lui ? Loin de moi ! Que le roi ne mette rien à la charge de son serviteur [ni] de toute la maison de mon père, car ton serviteur ne savait rien de tout cela, ni petite ni grande chose. »
fr.B: Est-ce aujourd’hui la première fois que j’ai consulté Dieu pour lui ? Loin de moi une telle pensée ! Que le roi n’accuse de rien son serviteur ni personne de la famille de mon père, car ton serviteur ne savait absolument rien de cette affaire, ni petite ni grande chose. »
fr.R: Ce n’était pas la première fois que je demandais à Dieu de guider David. Jamais je ne comploterais contre toi ! Je t’en prie, mon roi, ne m’accuse pas, ni personne de ma famille. Je ne savais rien du tout de cette affaire. »

vi.L: Hôm nay tôi mới bắt đầu cầu hỏi Đức Chúa Trời cho người sao? Không đời nào! Xin vua đừng quy tội gì cho đầy tớ của vua [hay] cho cả nhà cha tôi, vì đầy tớ của vua không biết gì về tất cả việc này, dù nhỏ hay lớn."
vi.B: Đây đâu phải là lần đầu tiên tôi cầu hỏi Đức Chúa Trời cho ông ấy? Tôi chẳng hề có ý gì khác! Xin bệ hạ đừng buộc tội đầy tớ của bệ hạ hay bất cứ ai trong gia đình cha tôi, vì đầy tớ của bệ hạ không hề biết gì về việc này, dù nhỏ hay lớn."
vi.R: Đây không phải là lần đầu tôi cầu hỏi Đức Chúa Trời để hướng dẫn Đa-vít. Tôi không bao giờ âm mưu chống lại vua! Thưa đức vua, xin đừng buộc tội tôi hay bất cứ ai trong gia đình tôi. Tôi chẳng biết gì về chuyện này cả."

decisions.choice: did I begin today to inquire: no, I had done so before
decisions.reason: The question expects "no". Asking God's guidance for David, the king's own commander, was nothing new, so it cannot be evidence of a plot.

decisions.choice: far be it from me: I would never do such a thing
alternatives: far be it from me that this was the first time
decisions.reason: The phrase is a strong denial, "that would be unthinkable for me" (12:23; 14:45). Ahimelech rejects the charge of conspiring against the king.

decisions.choice: small or great: nothing at all
decisions.reason: Naming the two extremes covers everything in between (20:2). Ahimelech knew nothing of any quarrel between Saul and David, which agrees with chapter 21, where David told him he was on the king's business (21:3).

decisions.choice: his servant ... your servant: Ahimelech speaks of himself humbly
decisions.reason: Speaking of oneself as "your servant" in the third person was the polite way to address a king.

decisions.choice: me ... I would never plot against you
decisions.reason: Readable uses "me" and "I" for the polite "your servant", and spells out what Ahimelech denies. It adds "my king" to keep the respectful tone.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מ֥וֹת תָּמ֖וּת אֲחִימֶ֑לֶךְ אַתָּ֖ה וְכָל־בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the king, dying you shall die, Ahimelech, you and all [the] house of your father.

en.L: And the king said, "You shall surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father's house."
en.B: But the king said, "You will certainly die, Ahimelech, you and your father's whole family."
en.R: But the king said, "Ahimelech, you will die! You and all your relatives will be put to death."

es.L: Y dijo el rey: «De cierto morirás, Ahimelec, tú y toda la casa de tu padre».
es.B: Pero el rey dijo: «Morirás sin remedio, Ahimelec, tú y toda la familia de tu padre».
es.R: Pero el rey dijo: «¡Ahimelec, vas a morir! Tú y todos tus parientes {{plural_you:van|vais}} a morir».

fr.L: Et le roi dit : « Tu mourras certainement, Ahimélek, toi et toute la maison de ton père. »
fr.B: Mais le roi dit : « Tu vas mourir, Ahimélek, toi et toute la famille de ton père. »
fr.R: Mais le roi a dit : « Ahimélek, tu vas mourir ! Toi et toute ta famille, vous serez mis à mort. »

vi.L: Vua nói: "A-hi-mê-léc, ngươi chắc chắn phải chết, ngươi và cả nhà cha ngươi."
vi.B: Nhưng vua nói: "A-hi-mê-léc, ngươi chắc chắn phải chết, ngươi và cả gia đình cha ngươi."
vi.R: Nhưng vua nói: "A-hi-mê-léc, ngươi phải chết! Ngươi và tất cả bà con ngươi đều phải bị xử tử."

decisions.choice: dying you shall die: a certain sentence of death
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. It is the form of a death sentence, the same words Saul spoke against his own son Jonathan (14:44).

decisions.choice: all your father's house: the whole family punished
decisions.reason: Saul condemns not only Ahimelech but the whole priestly family, though the law of Moses forbade putting children to death for a father's sin (Deuteronomy 24:16).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ לָרָצִים֩ הַנִּצָּבִ֨ים עָלָ֜יו סֹ֥בּוּ וְהָמִ֣יתוּ׀כֹּהֲנֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה כִּ֤י גַם־יָדָם֙ עִם־דָּוִ֔ד וְכִ֤י יָֽדְעוּ֙ כִּֽי־בֹרֵ֣חַ ה֔וּא וְלֹ֥א גָל֖וּ אֶת־אָזְנִ֑י וְלֹֽא־אָב֞וּ עַבְדֵ֤י הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לִשְׁלֹ֣חַ אֶת־יָדָ֔ם לִפְגֹ֖עַ בְּכֹהֲנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said the king to the runners [who were] standing by him, turn and put to death [the] priests of Yahweh, for also their hand [is] with David, and for they knew that fleeing [was] he, and not they uncovered my ear. And not were willing [the] servants of the king to stretch out their hand to strike against [the] priests of Yahweh.

en.L: And the king said to the runners who [were] standing by him, "Turn and put to death the priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because their hand also [is] with David, and because they knew that he was fleeing and did not uncover my ear." But the servants of the king were not willing to stretch out their hand to strike the priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Then the king said to the guards who stood around him, "Turn and kill the priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because they too have sided with David. They knew he was running away, and they did not tell me." But the king's officials refused to lift a hand to strike down the priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Then the king told the guards standing around him, "Go and kill the priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! They are on David's side too. They knew he was running away from me, but they did not tell me." But the king's officials would not lift a hand to attack the priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y dijo el rey a los corredores que estaban de pie junto a él: «{{plural_you:Vuélvanse y maten|Volveos y matad}} a los sacerdotes {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, porque también su mano [está] con David, y porque sabían que él huía y no descubrieron mi oído». Pero los siervos del rey no quisieron extender su mano para herir a los sacerdotes {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Luego el rey les dijo a los guardias que estaban a su alrededor: «{{plural_you:Vuélvanse y maten|Volveos y matad}} a los sacerdotes {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, porque también ellos se han puesto de parte de David. Sabían que él estaba huyendo y no me lo dijeron». Pero los oficiales del rey se negaron a levantar la mano contra los sacerdotes {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Entonces el rey les dijo a los guardias que estaban a su alrededor: «¡{{plural_you:Vayan y maten|Id y matad}} a los sacerdotes {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}! Ellos también están del lado de David. Sabían que huía de mí, pero no me lo dijeron». Pero los oficiales del rey no quisieron levantar la mano para atacar a los sacerdotes {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et le roi dit aux coureurs qui se tenaient près de lui : « Tournez-vous et faites mourir les prêtres {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, car leur main aussi [est] avec David, et parce qu’ils savaient qu’il s’enfuyait et ne m’ont pas découvert l’oreille. » Mais les serviteurs du roi ne voulurent pas étendre la main pour frapper les prêtres {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Puis le roi dit aux gardes qui l’entouraient : « Avancez et tuez les prêtres {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, car eux aussi ont pris le parti de David. Ils savaient qu’il s’enfuyait, et ils ne m’ont rien dit. » Mais les officiers du roi refusèrent de lever la main pour frapper les prêtres {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Ensuite, le roi a dit aux gardes qui étaient autour de lui : « Allez tuer les prêtres {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ! Eux aussi sont du côté de David. Ils savaient qu’il s’enfuyait loin de moi, mais ils ne me l’ont pas dit. » Mais les officiers du roi n’ont pas voulu lever la main pour attaquer les prêtres {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.

vi.L: Vua nói với các lính chạy [trước vua] đang đứng quanh mình: "Hãy quay lại giết các thầy tế lễ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, vì tay họ cũng [ở] với Đa-vít, và vì họ biết nó chạy trốn mà không mở tai cho ta." Nhưng các đầy tớ của vua không chịu giơ tay đánh các thầy tế lễ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Rồi vua bảo các vệ binh đứng chung quanh: "Hãy quay lại giết các thầy tế lễ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, vì chúng cũng theo phe Đa-vít. Chúng biết nó trốn mà không báo cho ta." Nhưng các quần thần của vua không chịu giơ tay hại các thầy tế lễ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Rồi vua bảo các vệ binh đứng chung quanh: "Hãy đi giết các thầy tế lễ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}! Chúng cũng theo phe Đa-vít. Chúng biết nó đang chạy trốn ta mà không báo cho ta." Nhưng các quần thần của vua không chịu ra tay tấn công các thầy tế lễ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

decisions.choice: the runners: the king's guard
decisions.reason: "Runners" were the soldiers who ran ahead of the king's chariot and guarded him (8:11; 2 Samuel 15:1). They carried out his orders.

decisions.choice: their hand is with David: they are on David's side
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for help and support. Saul claims the priests have taken David's side against him.

decisions.choice: the king's servants refuse: they will not kill the priests of Yahweh
decisions.reason: The guards disobey a direct order from the king rather than strike men who serve Yahweh. The phrase "priests of Yahweh" at both ends of the verse stresses whose servants Saul wants killed.

decisions.choice: strike against: attack and kill
decisions.reason: The verb means "fall upon" or "strike", and is used of an attack meant to kill (verse 18; 2 Samuel 1:15).

decisions.choice: the guards; the king's officials
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable call the runners "guards", which says what they did. The king's servants are "officials", as in verse 6; they are the same men standing around the king.

decisions.choice: los corredores (L); los guardias (B, R)
decisions.reason: The “runners” were the king's guard, who ran before his chariot (m1). Literal keeps the Hebrew word; Balanced and Readable say what they were, as the English (r-en-1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לְדוֹאֵ֔ג סֹ֣ב אַתָּ֔ה וּפְגַ֖ע בַּכֹּהֲנִ֑ים וַיִּסֹּ֞ב דּוֹאֵ֣ג הָאֲדֹמִ֗י וַיִּפְגַּע־הוּא֙ בַּכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים וַיָּ֣מֶת׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא שְׁמֹנִ֤ים וַחֲמִשָּׁה֙ אִ֔ישׁ נֹשֵׂ֖א אֵפ֥וֹד בָּֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the king to Doeg, turn you and fall on the priests. And turned Doeg the Edomite and fell he on the priests, and he killed on that day eighty and five man bearing an ephod of linen.

en.L: And the king said to Doeg, "You turn and fall upon the priests." And Doeg the Edomite turned, and he fell upon the priests, and he killed on that day eighty-five men bearing a linen ephod.
en.B: Then the king said to Doeg, "You turn and strike down the priests." So Doeg the Edomite turned and attacked the priests himself. On that day he put to death eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod.
en.R: So the king told Doeg, "Then you go and kill the priests!" Doeg, the man from Edom, went and attacked the priests. That day Doeg killed eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod, the clothing of priests.

es.L: Y dijo el rey a Doeg: «Vuélvete tú y arrójate sobre los sacerdotes». Y se volvió Doeg el edomita, y se arrojó él sobre los sacerdotes, y mató aquel día a ochenta y cinco hombres que llevaban efod de lino.
es.B: Entonces el rey le dijo a Doeg: «Vuélvete tú y derriba a los sacerdotes». Así que Doeg el edomita se volvió y él mismo atacó a los sacerdotes. Aquel día dio muerte a ochenta y cinco hombres que vestían el efod de lino.
es.R: Así que el rey le dijo a Doeg: «¡Entonces ve tú y mata a los sacerdotes!». Doeg, el hombre de Edom, fue y atacó a los sacerdotes. Aquel día Doeg mató a ochenta y cinco hombres que llevaban el efod de lino, la ropa de los sacerdotes.

fr.L: Et le roi dit à Doëg : « Toi, tourne-toi et jette-toi sur les prêtres. » Et Doëg l’Édomite se tourna, et lui se jeta sur les prêtres, et il tua ce jour-là quatre-vingt-cinq hommes qui portaient l’éphod de lin.
fr.B: Alors le roi dit à Doëg : « Toi, avance et abats les prêtres. » Doëg l’Édomite s’avança et attaqua lui-même les prêtres. Ce jour-là, il fit mourir quatre-vingt-cinq hommes qui portaient l’éphod de lin.
fr.R: Alors le roi a dit à Doëg : « Eh bien, toi, va tuer les prêtres ! » Doëg, l’homme d’Édom, est allé attaquer les prêtres. Ce jour-là, Doëg a tué quatre-vingt-cinq hommes qui portaient l’éphod de lin, le vêtement des prêtres.

vi.L: Vua nói với Đô-e: "Ngươi hãy quay lại xông vào các thầy tế lễ." Đô-e người Ê-đôm quay lại, chính hắn xông vào các thầy tế lễ, và trong ngày đó hắn giết tám mươi lăm người mặc áo ê-phót bằng vải gai.
vi.B: Vua bảo Đô-e: "Ngươi hãy quay lại giết các thầy tế lễ." Vậy Đô-e người Ê-đôm quay lại, tự tay tấn công các thầy tế lễ. Trong ngày đó hắn giết tám mươi lăm người mặc áo ê-phót bằng vải gai.
vi.R: Vậy vua bảo Đô-e: "Thế thì ngươi hãy đi giết các thầy tế lễ!" Đô-e, người Ê-đôm, liền đi tấn công các thầy tế lễ. Hôm đó Đô-e giết tám mươi lăm người mặc áo ê-phót bằng vải gai, là áo của thầy tế lễ.

decisions.choice: eighty-five: the number in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation gives the number as 305, and it also lacks the word "linen". The Hebrew number is followed here. Either way, nearly all the priestly family were killed.

decisions.choice: bearing a linen ephod: wearing the priest's linen garment
decisions.reason: The linen ephod was a simple garment worn by priests when serving, as the boy Samuel wore one (2:18). It is not the special ephod kept at Nob for asking God's will (21:10). The phrase marks the dead as serving priests.

decisions.choice: you ... he: Doeg himself does what the others refused
decisions.reason: The pronouns "you" and "he" are added for emphasis. Saul turns to the foreigner, and Doeg alone is willing to kill the priests.

decisions.choice: Doeg the Edomite: the man named in the title of Psalm 52
decisions.reason: The title of Psalm 52 (52:2 in the Hebrew numbering) links that psalm to the time when Doeg the Edomite went and told Saul that David had come to Ahimelech's house.

decisions.choice: Doeg: the marginal spelling
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text spell the name in a slightly longer form here and in verse 22. The scribes' note in the margin gives the usual spelling, Doeg. It is the same man.

decisions.choice: strike down; attacked
decisions.reason: "Fall upon" means attack in order to kill. Literal keeps "fall upon"; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: the clothing of priests
decisions.reason: Readable adds a short explanation so the reader knows the linen ephod marked these men as priests (see the meaning decision on the ephod).

decisions.choice: the narrator calls Doeg "hắn" from the moment he kills the priests
decisions.reason: The man who strikes down the priests of the LORD is spoken of as a wrongdoer, as Goliath was.

source.text: וְאֵ֨ת נֹ֤ב עִיר־הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ הִכָּ֣ה לְפִי־חֶ֔רֶב מֵאִישׁ֙ וְעַד־אִשָּׁ֔ה מֵעוֹלֵ֖ל וְעַד־יוֹנֵ֑ק וְשׁ֧וֹר וַחֲמ֛וֹר וָשֶׂ֖ה לְפִי־חָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And Nob, [the] city of the priests, he struck to [the] mouth of [the] sword, from man and to woman, from child and to nursing infant, and ox and donkey and sheep, to [the] mouth of [the] sword.

en.L: And Nob, the city of the priests, he struck with the edge of the sword, from man to woman, from child to nursing infant, and ox and donkey and sheep, with the edge of the sword.
en.B: He also put Nob, the town of the priests, to the sword. Men and women, children and babies, oxen, donkeys and sheep, he killed them all with the sword.
en.R: Then he attacked Nob, the town where the priests lived. He killed everyone there with the sword: men and women, children and babies. He even killed the cattle, donkeys and sheep.

es.L: Y a Nob, la ciudad de los sacerdotes, la hirió a filo de espada, desde el hombre hasta la mujer, desde el niño hasta el bebé de pecho, y buey y asno y oveja, a filo de espada.
es.B: También pasó a filo de espada a Nob, la ciudad de los sacerdotes. Hombres y mujeres, niños y bebés, bueyes, asnos y ovejas: a todos los mató a espada.
es.R: Después atacó Nob, el pueblo donde vivían los sacerdotes. Mató a espada a todos los que había allí: hombres y mujeres, niños y bebés. Mató hasta las vacas, los burros y las ovejas.

fr.L: Et Nob, la ville des prêtres, il la frappa du tranchant de l’épée, de l’homme à la femme, de l’enfant au nourrisson, et bœuf, et âne, et mouton, du tranchant de l’épée.
fr.B: Il passa aussi au fil de l’épée Nob, la ville des prêtres. Hommes et femmes, enfants et nourrissons, bœufs, ânes et moutons, il les tua tous par l’épée.
fr.R: Ensuite, il a attaqué Nob, la ville où habitaient les prêtres. Il a tué tout le monde avec l’épée : les hommes et les femmes, les enfants et les bébés. Il a même tué les bœufs, les ânes et les moutons.

vi.L: Hắn đánh Nóp, thành của các thầy tế lễ, bằng lưỡi gươm, từ đàn ông đến đàn bà, từ trẻ con đến trẻ đang bú, cả bò, lừa và chiên, bằng lưỡi gươm.
vi.B: Hắn cũng dùng gươm tàn sát Nóp, thành của các thầy tế lễ. Đàn ông, đàn bà, trẻ con, trẻ sơ sinh, bò, lừa và chiên, hắn đều giết sạch bằng gươm.
vi.R: Rồi hắn tấn công Nóp, là thành các thầy tế lễ sinh sống. Hắn dùng gươm giết hết mọi người ở đó: đàn ông, đàn bà, trẻ em và trẻ sơ sinh. Hắn giết cả bò, lừa và chiên nữa.

decisions.choice: he struck: Doeg, acting on Saul's orders
decisions.reason: The subject is not named. It follows on from Doeg in verse 18, but the slaughter was Saul's doing, and verse 21 says "Saul had killed the priests". The text may mean Doeg with men under him, or Saul through his men.

decisions.choice: to the mouth of the sword: with the edge of the sword, killing everyone
decisions.reason: The sword is pictured as a mouth that devours. The phrase means killing without sparing anyone.

decisions.choice: man, woman, child, infant, ox, donkey, sheep: the destruction Saul refused to carry out on Amalek
decisions.reason: The list matches the command Saul was given against Amalek (15:3). There he spared the king and the best animals (15:9); here he wipes out a town of Yahweh's own priests.

decisions.choice: he killed them all
decisions.reason: Balanced repeats the verb at the end to hold the long list together.

source.text: וַיִּמָּלֵ֣ט בֵּן־אֶחָ֗ד לַאֲחִימֶ֨לֶךְ֙ בֶּן־אֲחִט֔וּב וּשְׁמ֖וֹ אֶבְיָתָ֑ר וַיִּבְרַ֖ח אַחֲרֵ֥י דָוִֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And escaped one son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub, and his name [was] Abiathar, and he fled after David.

en.L: And one son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped, and his name [was] Abiathar, and he fled after David.
en.B: But one son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub, whose name was Abiathar, escaped and fled to join David.
en.R: But one of Ahimelech's sons got away. His name was Abiathar, and he went to join David.

es.L: Y escapó un hijo de Ahimelec hijo de Ahitob, y su nombre [era] Abiatar, y huyó tras David.
es.B: Pero un hijo de Ahimelec hijo de Ahitob, llamado Abiatar, escapó y huyó para unirse a David.
es.R: Pero uno de los hijos de Ahimelec se escapó. Se llamaba Abiatar, y se fue a unirse a David.

fr.L: Et un fils d’Ahimélek, fils d’Ahitoub, s’échappa ; son nom [était] Abiathar, et il s’enfuit à la suite de David.
fr.B: Mais un fils d’Ahimélek, fils d’Ahitoub, nommé Abiathar, réussit à s’échapper et s’enfuit pour rejoindre David.
fr.R: Mais un des fils d’Ahimélek a réussi à s’échapper. Il s’appelait Abiathar, et il est allé rejoindre David.

vi.L: Một người con trai của A-hi-mê-léc con trai A-hi-túp thoát được, tên [là] A-bi-a-tha, và ông chạy trốn theo Đa-vít.
vi.B: Nhưng một người con trai của A-hi-mê-léc con trai A-hi-túp, tên là A-bi-a-tha, trốn thoát và chạy đến với Đa-vít.
vi.R: Nhưng một người con trai của A-hi-mê-léc thoát được. Ông tên là A-bi-a-tha, và ông đến theo Đa-vít.

decisions.choice: Abiathar: the priest who served David
decisions.reason: Abiathar brought the ephod with him (23:6) and served as David's priest for the rest of his reign (2 Samuel 8:17; 15:24-29). Solomon later removed him from the priesthood, and the narrator links that to the word against Eli's house (1 Kings 2:26-27).

decisions.choice: fled after David: fled to join David
decisions.reason: "After" here means following David to be with him, not chasing him.

decisions.choice: one of Ahimelech's sons
decisions.reason: Readable leaves out "son of Ahitub", already given in verses 9 and 11, to keep the sentence short.

source.text: וַיַּגֵּ֥ד אֶבְיָתָ֖ר לְדָוִ֑ד כִּ֚י הָרַ֣ג שָׁא֔וּל אֵ֖ת כֹּהֲנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And told Abiathar to David that had killed Saul [the] priests of Yahweh.

en.L: And Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Abiathar reported to David that Saul had killed the priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Abiathar told David that Saul had put the priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to death.

es.L: Y contó Abiatar a David que Saúl había matado a los sacerdotes {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Abiatar le informó a David que Saúl había matado a los sacerdotes {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Abiatar le contó a David que Saúl había mandado matar a los sacerdotes {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et Abiathar apprit à David que Saül avait tué les prêtres {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Abiathar annonça à David que Saül avait tué les prêtres {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Abiathar a raconté à David que Saül avait fait mourir les prêtres {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.

vi.L: A-bi-a-tha báo cho Đa-vít rằng Sau-lơ đã giết các thầy tế lễ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: A-bi-a-tha báo cho Đa-vít biết Sau-lơ đã giết các thầy tế lễ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: A-bi-a-tha kể cho Đa-vít rằng Sau-lơ đã giết các thầy tế lễ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

decisions.choice: Saul had killed: Saul is held responsible
decisions.reason: Doeg did the killing, but Abiathar names Saul, who gave the order. The guilt is the king's.

records.literal_gloss: And said David to Abiathar, I knew on that day, that there [was] Doeg the Edomite, that surely he would tell Saul. I have turned in every soul of [the] house of your father.

en.L: And David said to Abiathar, "I knew on that day, because Doeg the Edomite [was] there, that he would surely tell Saul. I have brought [this] around against every life of your father's house.
en.B: David said to Abiathar, "That day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, I knew he would be sure to tell Saul. I am to blame for the death of every person in your father's family.
en.R: David said to Abiathar, "That day I saw Doeg from Edom there, and I knew he would be sure to tell Saul. It is my fault that everyone in your father's family was killed.

es.L: Y dijo David a Abiatar: «Yo sabía aquel día, porque Doeg el edomita [estaba] allí, que de cierto se lo diría a Saúl. Yo he ocasionado [esto] contra toda vida de la casa de tu padre.
es.B: David le dijo a Abiatar: «Aquel día, cuando vi allí a Doeg el edomita, supe que sin duda se lo contaría a Saúl. Yo tengo la culpa de la muerte de todas las personas de la familia de tu padre.
es.R: David le dijo a Abiatar: «Aquel día vi allí a Doeg, el de Edom, y supe que se lo iba a contar a Saúl. Es culpa mía que hayan matado a toda la familia de tu padre.

fr.L: Et David dit à Abiathar : « Je savais ce jour-là, puisque Doëg l’Édomite [était] là, qu’il ne manquerait pas de le rapporter à Saül. C’est moi qui ai causé [la perte] de toutes les vies de la maison de ton père.
fr.B: David dit à Abiathar : « Ce jour-là, quand j’ai vu Doëg l’Édomite, je savais qu’il ne manquerait pas d’avertir Saül. C’est moi qui suis responsable de la mort de toute la famille de ton père.
fr.R: David a dit à Abiathar : « Ce jour-là, j’ai vu Doëg l’Édomite, et je savais qu’il irait sûrement tout raconter à Saül. C’est de ma faute si toute la famille de ton père a été tuée.

vi.L: Đa-vít nói với A-bi-a-tha: "Ngày hôm đó, vì Đô-e người Ê-đôm [có mặt] ở đó, tôi đã biết chắc hắn sẽ báo cho Sau-lơ. Chính tôi đã gây ra [cái chết] cho mọi người trong nhà cha anh.
vi.B: Đa-vít nói với A-bi-a-tha: "Hôm đó, khi thấy Đô-e người Ê-đôm có mặt ở đó, tôi biết chắc hắn sẽ báo cho Sau-lơ. Tôi phải chịu trách nhiệm về cái chết của mọi người trong gia đình cha anh.
vi.R: Đa-vít nói với A-bi-a-tha: "Hôm đó tôi thấy Đô-e người Ê-đôm ở đó, và tôi biết chắc hắn sẽ báo cho Sau-lơ. Chính vì tôi mà mọi người trong gia đình cha anh bị giết.

decisions.choice: surely he would tell: the verb doubled for certainty
decisions.reason: David knew at the time that Doeg would report what he saw. The doubled verb shows that it was certain.

decisions.choice: I have turned against every life: I have caused the death of all of them
alternatives: I am guilty of the lives of
decisions.reason: The verb means "turn" or "bring around", and with "against" it means to be the cause of what happened to someone. The ancient Greek translation has "I am guilty", which may come from a slightly different word. Both say that David takes the blame.

decisions.choice: every life: every person
decisions.reason: The word often translated "soul" here means a living person, a life.

decisions.choice: I am to blame for the death of (Balanced); It is my fault (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew picture of "turning" against someone does not work in English, so Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: David says "tôi" and "anh" to Abiathar
decisions.reason: David speaks to the young priest who has lost his family as to a companion; a reviewer may prefer "ông" for a priest.

records.literal_gloss: Stay with me; do not fear, for [he] who seeks my life seeks your life, for [in] safekeeping you [are] with me.

en.L: Stay with me; do not be afraid, for he who seeks my life seeks your life, for you [are] in safekeeping with me."
en.B: Stay with me and do not be afraid. The one who is after my life is after yours as well. With me you will be kept safe."
en.R: Stay with me, and do not be afraid. The man who wants to kill me also wants to kill you. You will be safe here with me."

es.L: Quédate conmigo; no temas, porque el que busca mi vida busca tu vida; pues conmigo [estarás] bajo custodia».
es.B: Quédate conmigo y no tengas miedo. El que anda tras mi vida anda también tras la tuya. Conmigo estarás a salvo».
es.R: Quédate conmigo y no tengas miedo. El hombre que quiere matarme también quiere matarte a ti. Aquí conmigo estarás seguro».

fr.L: Reste avec moi ; n’aie pas peur, car celui qui cherche ma vie cherche ta vie ; car tu [seras] bien gardé auprès de moi. »
fr.B: Reste avec moi et n’aie pas peur. Celui qui en veut à ma vie en veut aussi à la tienne. Avec moi, tu seras en sécurité. »
fr.R: Reste avec moi et n’aie pas peur. L’homme qui veut me tuer veut aussi te tuer. Avec moi, tu seras en sécurité. »

vi.L: Hãy ở với tôi; đừng sợ, vì kẻ tìm hại mạng sống tôi cũng tìm hại mạng sống anh; anh [sẽ] được bảo vệ khi ở với tôi."
vi.B: Hãy ở lại với tôi, đừng sợ. Kẻ muốn lấy mạng tôi cũng muốn lấy mạng anh. Ở với tôi, anh sẽ được an toàn."
vi.R: Hãy ở lại với tôi và đừng sợ. Kẻ muốn giết tôi cũng muốn giết anh. Ở đây với tôi, anh sẽ được an toàn."

decisions.choice: seeks my life: wants to kill me
decisions.reason: To seek someone's life is to try to kill him (20:1). The one who seeks both lives is Saul, though David does not name him.

decisions.choice: safekeeping: being guarded, kept safe
decisions.reason: The word means a watch or guard, or something placed in someone's care. David promises to protect Abiathar as one entrusted to him.

decisions.choice: is after my life
decisions.reason: Balanced uses an everyday phrase for "seeks my life"; Readable says plainly "wants to kill".
